Config is frozen (immutable after construction)

Tests import DDL from here — no inline DDL in test files. proj_tasks.db's tables (open_tasks, task_events, commit_task_map, task_edges) and migrate_tasks_db were removed (task:87ec7876) along with src/tools/tasks.py, the actual production path that created them — this module's docstring always said those constants existed only for tests and one-time install.

This module is not the production schema/migration path for the DBs it still covers

contracts: Reads hook payload from stdin, writes JSON to stdout
Returns additionalSystemPrompt for UserPromptSubmit
Returns permissionDecision=deny for blocked PreToolUse
PreToolUse handlers may also return permissionDecision=allow with additionalContext to inject a non-blocking reminder into Claude's context without denying the tool call
dispatcher-hook-event-routing.description: Single entry point for all Claude Code hook events. Routes each event type (UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionStart, SessionEnd) to its dedicated handler via a dispatch table.
invariants: Every hook event must map to exactly one handler in _HANDLERS
PreToolUse handlers that fail on irreversible tools must deny, not allow
Handlers return None to pass through or a dict with hookSpecificOutput to act

Two distinct PreToolUse response categories: gates (deny-capable checks like _check_task_body_format, run_gate) must resolve to a strict allow/deny decision; reminders (like _maybe_tmux_nudge for Bash) are allow-only and use additionalContext to surface non-blocking context — reminders never deny

Two distinct handler return shapes exist: PreToolUse/UserPromptSubmit handlers return None or a dict wrapping hookSpecificOutput; Stop handlers (_handle_stop) return None or a plain top-level {"decision": "block", "reason": ...} dict per Claude Code's Stop-hook schema (not wrapped in hookSpecificOutput). The turn-completion chime no longer uses Stop-hook blocking: since 150df2a the sound plays server-side via PlaySoundNode (detached afplay subprocess, start_new_session=True — no Claude round-trip). NoopNode marks the first Stop of a turn by setting state['stop_alert_sent']=True, which gates PlaySoundNode (next node in the stop chain) so the chime fires exactly once per turn; sound_played guards replays within the same turn, and run_session() resets stop_alert_sent=False on the next UserPromptSubmit. run_stop() in session_graph.py still surfaces-and-clears pending_hook_output for any node that sets one (task:aacf3ef3 history; refactored by 150df2a).

The drift-reflection nudge (_maybe_drift_reflection_nudge, fired every 8th Write/Edit/MultiEdit under an active task, read from the session checkpoint) was removed here and ported to task-framework as taskfw.dispatcher.drift_reflection_nudge (task:f1d46386) — task-framework owns the active task since commit 6633bf1 deleted claude-hooks' langchain_learning task nodes (activate_task.py, load_related_tasks, log_task_events) on that basis. Do not re-add a claude-hooks-side drift/north-star nudge; task-framework is the one owner of active-task state and any reminder derived from it.

The Execution Contract (activate_task.py._build_execution_contract, a fixed philosophy block rendered every turn via _format_system_prompt while a task was active) died with the same 6633bf1 deletion and has no live equivalent anywhere as of task:f1d46386 — it is not merely moved, unlike the drift nudge.
dispatcher-hook-event-routing.name: dispatcher-hook-event-routing

contracts: Returns a string (may be empty) to be injected as additionalSystemPrompt
All sections are markdown-formatted
dispatcher-system-prompt-assembly.description: Assembles the UserPromptSubmit additionalSystemPrompt from SessionState context (memories, task context, related tasks/commits, rag chunks) into markdown sections, applying a token budget before rendering.
invariants: Sections are only emitted when their data is non-empty

Related tasks section is populated when LoadRelatedTasksNode finds semantically similar done tasks via TurboVec neighbor search (capped at 3); empty when no active task, no rag index, or no matching done neighbors
Task context summary takes precedence over raw task history when both exist

New-project note is emitted when ctx['cwd_unmapped'] is true (set by CwdDomainDetectNode only on the first turn a session's cwd is unmapped, tracked via cwd_domain_reminder_sent in checkpoint state so it fires once per session, not every turn)

Before assembly, _enforce_context_budget(ctx) trims ctx['memories'] from the tail (lowest-scored, since the list is pre-sorted descending) until the combined token count of memories+task_memories+related_tasks+related_commits+task_rag_chunks fits _CONTEXT_TOKEN_BUDGET (4000 tokens), or memories is empty. task_memories/related_tasks/related_commits/task_rag_chunks are counted toward the budget but never trimmed themselves — they're already small/capped by their producing nodes.

task_body is hard-truncated to _TASK_BODY_CHAR_CAP (3000 chars) at render time, appending an "...[truncated]" marker when cut — it has no upstream length cap (a task's body can be arbitrarily long, e.g. a large epic scaffold).

mid_task_decisions (Task decisions section) is capped to the most recent _MAX_DECISIONS (15) entries by langchain_learning/nodes/decision_task.py, sliced on every tasks__add_decision append — not trimmed in dispatcher.py itself. This checkpoint state exists solely for prompt injection; the durable decision history lives in the task's DB record, unaffected by the slice.

execution_contract is rendered as its own section, independent of task_body and _enforce_context_budget — it is NOT subject to _TASK_BODY_CHAR_CAP truncation or memories-budget eviction, by design (a fixed north-star template built once at task activation by activate_task.py._build_execution_contract, must stay byte-identical every turn). Cleared alongside the other active-task fields at all three deactivation sites: DeactivateTaskNode (tasks__clear_active/tasks__finish), ActivateTaskNode's pop-to-empty-stack, and LogTaskEventsNode's "task:<id> done" auto-close (task:eb46ac47 — this third site was originally missed).

After _format_system_prompt, the UPS handler appends one-shot node output: if ctx['pending_hook_output'].hookSpecificOutput has hookEventName == 'UserPromptSubmit', its additionalContext is appended to the assembled system prompt (e.g. LogTaskEventsNode's /task-introspection nudge after a "task:<id> done" auto-close, task:eb46ac47). run_session() surfaces-and-clears the checkpoint copy (mirroring run_post_tool/run_stop), so the payload renders exactly once and cannot leak into the next PostToolUse response; the hookEventName gate prevents a stale cross-event payload from ever being rendered here.

The '## Repo memories' section and repo_task_memories (task:850ddd65's per-repo memory split) were removed by task:a7ddc132 — task_memories now always comes from the global MEMORY.sqlite scorer, with no per-repo alternative source.
dispatcher-system-prompt-assembly.name: dispatcher-system-prompt-assembly

contracts: Returns (True, reason) for commits missing task:<id> in both the command string and any -F/--file target
Returns (False, '') for all non-commit Bash calls, including calls that merely contain the words git and commit in unrelated segments
Returns (False, '') when task:<id> is found in the command string OR inside a file passed via -F/--file
A missing or unreadable -F file is treated as no match (deny), not a crash

Detection catches `git commit`, `git -C <path> commit`, `git --no-pager commit`, commits behind wrappers (sudo/env/time/nohup) or leading VAR=value assignments, commits after a leading `cd ... &&`, and git_local.sh
gates-commit-traceability.description: GitCommitGate enforces that every version-control commit (via Bash or the MCP tool) includes a task:<id> reference for traceability. Commit DETECTION is per shell segment and command-word based (_is_git_commit / _segment_is_git_commit, task:e247268e): the command is split on newline / ; / && / || / | / parens, and a segment counts only if its leading token is `git` (with global flags skipped before reading the subcommand) or a path whose basename is git_local.sh. The task:<id> SEARCH still runs against the whole command string, not per segment, because heredoc messages put the id on a different line from the invocation. The reference may instead live in a file named via -F/--file (git commit -F <path>) — the form task-framework's own /commit skill recommends for multi-paragraph messages, since heredocs and -m chains mangle them.
invariants: Every commit must reference task:<id> somewhere the gate can see — the command string or a -F/--file target, not necessarily the command string alone

Non-commit Bash calls are never blocked by this gate. This is now true by construction rather than by intent: detection asks whether a shell segment's COMMAND WORD is git/git_local.sh, so the words appearing inside an echo, a string literal, or a shell comment cannot trigger it. Before task:e247268e the regex bridged shell separators and newlines, and denied things like `git status` followed by `echo "nothing to commit"`.

_segment_is_git_commit never raises: shlex.split throws ValueError on the unbalanced quotes that heredocs and $(...) fragments routinely produce, so it falls back to a plain split. A gate that denies Bash must degrade rather than except, or one malformed command breaks every Bash call.

hooks/server_memory.py's record_tool_from_hook shares this detector by importing _is_git_commit — it is the second consumer, and it inherited the same false positives until task:e247268e. Changing detection changes what lands on the session timeline as a 'git commit' event, not just what the gate blocks.
git_local.sh is matched on the segment's command word (basename), never as a substring anywhere in the command — otherwise `echo "git_local.sh"` reintroduces the false-positive class.
Gate logic runs inside a long-running uvicorn hooks.server:app process (port 8766) — editing hooks/gates.py has no effect until that process restarts; client.py is only a thin HTTP wrapper per call
gates-commit-traceability.name: gates-commit-traceability

contracts: check(tool, ctx) returns (deny: bool, reason: str)
deny=True means the tool must be blocked; reason is shown to Claude
gates-prereq-chain-enforcement.description: Anti-hallucination send-gate system. Verifies tool calls against session history before allowing them. Each gate is a composable chain of verifier factories loaded from gate_rules.yaml or hardcoded subclasses.
invariants: Gates operate only on tool call records written by the hook infrastructure, never on model memory
External gate rules from gate_rules.yaml never override internal Python gates
All gates fail open on DB errors — a broken gate never blocks tools
gates-prereq-chain-enforcement.name: gates-prereq-chain-enforcement

contracts: Callers reading hook_logs (e.g. hooks__read_logs_sqlite MCP tool) should treat it as a rolling ~40-50k row window of recent activity, not a complete historical log -- older entries are permanently gone once pruned, not archived.
hook-logs-sqlite-autoprune-at-50k.description: SQLiteHandler.emit() writes every log record to hook_logs in claude_hooks.sqlite (iCloud-synced), then checks COUNT(*) on every single insert. Once the table reaches 50,000 rows, it prunes down to the newest 40,000 rows in one DELETE, keyed by ts DESC (not id DESC).
invariants: hook_logs is capped at 50,000 rows -- it auto-prunes to 40,000 on the insert that crosses the threshold, so the table oscillates between ~40k and 50k rows over time, never growing unbounded.
Pruning keeps the newest rows by ts (timestamp), not by id/rowid -- id values become non-contiguous after a prune, so id (or max(id)) is not a valid proxy for total row count or table age.

The COUNT(*) check runs on every emit() call (every log line), not on a schedule/batch -- this is an O(n) check per write, acceptable at this volume but a scaling consideration if log volume grows sharply.
Pruning is silent -- emit() swallows all exceptions (bare except: pass), so a failed prune or count-check never surfaces as an error.
hook-logs-sqlite-autoprune-at-50k.name: hook-logs-sqlite-autoprune-at-50k

contracts: Usage: python3 client.py <HookEvent>
Reads hook payload JSON from stdin, POSTs to {CLAUDE_HOOKS_SERVER or http://127.0.0.1:8766}/hook/{EVENT}, prints the response JSON to stdout
Prints 'claude-hooks: client.py invoked for {EVENT}' to stderr on every invocation, regardless of success/failure
hooks-client-cwd-forwarding.description: Thin HTTP client for the FastAPI hook server. Reads the hook JSON payload from stdin (which already carries the real per-session cwd from Claude Code) and POSTs it to localhost:8766/hook/{event}.
invariants: CLAUDE_CWD env var is a fallback only, used when payload['cwd'] from stdin is missing/empty — it must never unconditionally overwrite a cwd Claude Code already supplied, since CLAUDE_CWD reflects whatever cwd the long-running server process happened to launch from, not the calling session's cwd (bug found 2026-07-08: unconditional overwrite clobbered every session's reported cwd with a stale/empty env var)
Fails open: if the server is unreachable, exits 0 with an empty JSON object rather than blocking the hook event

Every invocation prints a one-line 'claude-hooks: client.py invoked for {EVENT}' announcement to stderr immediately after EVENT is resolved, unconditionally (before the try/except) — this exists because server-side dispatcher logs only show the server's view, giving no signal that client.py itself ran for a given hook event (task:fb7d3777)
hooks-client-cwd-forwarding.name: hooks-client-cwd-forwarding

contracts: handle_server_memory(n_events) returns a markdown table or {error: ...}
handle_read_logs_sqlite(level, logger, search, limit, format="toon") returns a TOON-encoded string by default ("count: N\nrows[N]{...}:\n  ..."), or {count, rows} dict when format="json"
handle_session_id() returns {session_id, turn} or {error: ...} after one retry on empty first response

handle_checkpoint_query(thread_id="") returns {thread_id, turn_count, prompt_id, domains, keywords, memories, tool_hints, session_context, ...} or {error: ...}; thread_id doubles as session_id, omitted thread_id resolves to the current session via GET /session/current
hooks-mcp-tools-observability.description: MCP tools for querying hook state: server_memory (live chronological timeline via HTTP), checkpoint_query (thin HTTP wrapper over the live server's GET /session/{session_id}, reading in-process MemorySaver state — no longer a SQLite reader as of task:da29c842), and read_logs_sqlite (filtered log reader from claude_hooks.sqlite). Also session_id (added 2026-07-05, task:61703ef7): returns current session_id via GET /session/current with a built-in one-shot retry, absorbing the checkpoint-write race for a brand-new session.
evidence: tests/test_checkpoint_query_integration.py: live smoke test against the real running server
invariants: server_memory hits the live FastAPI server at 127.0.0.1:8766 — fails if server is down
read_logs_sqlite reads directly from iCloud DB path
session_id retries once (0.5s sleep) if the first /session/current response has no session_id — absorbs the race where a brand-new session's first checkpoint write lags behind the query

checkpoint_query is a thin HTTP wrapper over GET /session/{session_id} — it does NOT read ~/.claude/langgraph_checkpoints.db directly (that sqlite path was retired in production by task:b3964f85; the prior invariant here claiming checkpoint_query reads that file as 'the live DB SqliteSaver writes to in production' was true when confirmed 2026-07-05 (task:61703ef7) but went stale after task:b3964f85's later migration — corrected 2026-07-27, task:da29c842, after the stale assumption caused an unhandled 'no such table: checkpoints' error). checkpoint_query has no 'latest checkpoint across all threads' mode anymore — omitted thread_id resolves only to the current session, matching hooks__session_id's semantics.

read_logs_sqlite's `format` param defaults to "toon" (task:d2165715): rows share a uniform schema (id, ts, level, logger, message), which TOON's tabular header+rows encoding compresses well versus repeating JSON keys per row. format="json" is kept as an explicit fallback returning the original {count, rows} dict shape — callers needing the dict shape (e.g. programmatic filtering) must pass format="json" explicitly.

The TOON encoder itself (rows_to_toon/toon_cell) was extracted to src/toon.py (task:4b5bf21f) so src/tools/tasks.py's handle_list could reuse it — hooks.py now imports rows_to_toon rather than defining its own copy.

A docstring/comment's 'confirmed on <date>' claim is only as fresh as the last re-check against the code it describes — checkpoint_query's docstring cited a specific confirmation date (task:61703ef7) that read as settled fact but silently went stale after a later migration nobody circled back to update. Re-verify dated confirmations against current runtime behavior, don't trust the date alone.
hooks-mcp-tools-observability.name: hooks-mcp-tools-observability

contracts: __call__(state) -> {} always
load-active-task-pass-through.description: Pass-through node — active_task_id already lives in checkpoint state. Used to suppress the task for a turn when its project:<name> tag disagreed with the current cwd, reading proj_tasks.db to get the tag. That suppression, _project_from_cwd, and the _cfg import it needed were all removed (task:87ec7876): the tag was a guess derived from a working directory, and the lookup read a store this repo no longer owns. task-framework scopes the active task by workspace path directly, so what this approximated is now answered exactly by the system that owns it. The node now only logs.
invariants: Touches no database — returns {} unconditionally, active task or not
load-active-task-pass-through.name: load-active-task-pass-through

contracts: __call__(state) -> {prompt_tools, session_tools} state update
log-tool-usage-single-writer.description: Upserts a tool_hints.sqlite row per tool call and seeds keywords in the same connection. Used to also run _upsert_task_event_tools concurrently via a ThreadPoolExecutor, writing to task_events on EVERY tool call — removed (task:87ec7876) because task_events no longer exists. Found by grep for _cfg.tasks_db rather than the open_tasks/_connect patterns task:6240c675's sweep used, which is why it survived that earlier pass. With one writer left, the pool bought nothing; __call__ now calls _upsert_tool_hint directly.
invariants: Writes to tool_hints.sqlite only — no task store dependency
Test sessions (api-test-/test-/pytest- prefixes) skip the upsert entirely
log-tool-usage-single-writer.name: log-tool-usage-single-writer

contracts: setup(name) returns a logger with SQLiteHandler for hook scripts
get_logger(name) returns a 'lc.*' prefixed logger for the LCEL pipeline
logger-sqlite-handler.description: Shared SQLiteHandler that writes all hook and LangChain pipeline logs to claude_hooks.sqlite in iCloud. Singleton per DB path. Redirects to test DB when CLAUDE_HOOKS_TEST_LOG_DB env var is set. Auto-trims at 50k rows.
invariants: SQLiteHandler is a singleton per db_path — never creates duplicate handlers
emit() never raises — handleError() is a no-op
Log table is auto-trimmed to 40k rows when it exceeds 50k
Test redirect affects only the default singleton, not custom-path handlers
logger-sqlite-handler.name: logger-sqlite-handler

contracts: build_dispatcher(mcp) registers all tools from DOMAIN_MAP onto the FastMCP instance
mcp-dispatcher-domain-tool-map.description: FastMCP tool registry. Maps domain names to (module, [action]) pairs. Each action becomes an MCP tool named domain__action. All tool modules live under src/tools/. The 'tasks' entry was removed (task:87ec7876) along with tools/tasks.py — build_dispatcher imports every DOMAIN_MAP module unconditionally at startup, so a stale entry here would have broken server boot, not just one tool call.
invariants: Tool names follow domain__action convention
New tools require adding an entry to DOMAIN_MAP — no auto-discovery
Handler functions must be named handle_<action> in their module
Every DOMAIN_MAP entry's module must be importable — build_dispatcher loads all of them unconditionally at startup
mcp-dispatcher-domain-tool-map.name: mcp-dispatcher-domain-tool-map

contracts: mcp.run() starts the FastMCP server when invoked as __main__
mcp-server-bootstrap.description: MCP server entry point. Calls build_dispatcher to register all tools, then bootstraps by ensuring Ollama is running and rebuilding the task TurboVec embedding index if missing.
invariants: Ollama must be running for semantic task neighbor search to work
Task index is rebuilt at startup only if missing — not on every start
Bootstrap failures are logged and swallowed — never crash the server
mcp-server-bootstrap.name: mcp-server-bootstrap

contracts: Callers of score_memories() can add unbounded domains without any single domain silently excluding another from scoring, as long as no one domain individually exceeds batch_limit.
memory-scoring-per-domain-batch-limit.description: score_memories() fetches candidate memory rows per-domain (not one aggregate query across the whole memories table) before applying combination-signal scoring. Each distinct domain gets its own SELECT ... WHERE domain IS ? ORDER BY updated DESC LIMIT batch_limit, and the per-domain result sets are concatenated before scoring.
invariants: batch_limit (memory_scoring.json / src.config.memory_batch_limit) is a per-domain cap, not an aggregate cap across the whole memories table.
Truncation (when a domain exceeds batch_limit rows) always drops the stalest rows in that domain first, via ORDER BY updated DESC -- never an arbitrary rowid-order slice.
A small or new domain must never be starved out of the candidate pool by a large domain growing past batch_limit -- each domain is queried independently.
memory-scoring-per-domain-batch-limit.name: memory-scoring-per-domain-batch-limit

contracts: load_index(tvim_path, meta_path) returns (IdMapIndex | None, dict)
save_index(index, meta, tvim_path, meta_path) is atomic
query_index(index, meta, q_vec, k) returns list[dict] with id, score, plus meta fields
rag-core-turbovec-index.description: Generic TurboVec RAG core shared by code_rag and diff_rag. Provides load/save/query operations on IdMapIndex (.tvim) + .meta.json sidecar pairs. Atomic saves via tmp-then-rename. Callers supply precomputed query vectors.
invariants: Index and metadata sidecar are always written together atomically
load_index returns (None, {}) on any error — callers must handle missing index
query_index is stateless — no caching, no side effects
rag-core-turbovec-index.name: rag-core-turbovec-index

contracts: POST /hook/{event} calls dispatcher handler and returns hookSpecificOutput, a top-level decision/reason dict (Stop only), or {}
GET /health returns {status: ok}
GET /session/memory returns last N events from server_memory
GET /session/current returns {session_id, turn} from the most recent checkpoint — no active task required, unlike GET /session/active
_safe_json(request) -> dict — always returns a dict, never raises; malformed/empty/missing body returns {} with a logged warning
server-fastapi-hook-server.description: Persistent FastAPI server replacing per-invocation subprocess dispatcher. Routes POST /hook/{event} to dispatcher handlers. Uses MemorySaver (in-process, in-memory LangGraph checkpointer) — does NOT survive server restarts. Replaced SqliteSaver (task:b3964f85) after two corruption incidents. Per-thread checkpoint history is capped at 5000 rows, enforced from NoopNode on every Stop event. Single uvicorn worker process, event loop is uvloop (task:53c9f817). All 6 hook endpoints parse the request body via a shared _safe_json() helper (task:33419f95) that fails open to {} on malformed/empty JSON instead of raising — matches hooks/client.py's own fail-open design.
evidence: ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.debaditya.claude-hooks-pipeline.plist: uvicorn launch args, single process, no --workers
hooks/server.py: _safe_json() — shared JSON-parse helper used by all 6 /hook/{event} endpoints
invariants: Checkpoint state lives only in-process memory (MemorySaver) — discarded on every server restart/reload; nothing about session/task-activation state persists across a restart except what server_memory.py separately logs to SQLite
Per-thread checkpoint history is capped at 5000 rows via NoopNode on every Stop event, not by the server itself
Server runs on port 8766 as a single uvicorn worker process — deliberately not multi-worker/per-session
GET /session/active and GET /session/current both read live in-memory MemorySaver state (not a DB); /session/active requires an active task, /session/current does not
Event loop is uvloop, not stdlib asyncio — controlled entirely by whether uvloop is installed

All 6 /hook/{event} endpoints (UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionStart, SessionEnd) parse their body via the shared _safe_json(request) helper, which catches any JSON-parse failure and returns {} instead of letting it propagate to the generic exception handler as a 500 — found missing (task:33419f95, log audit 2026-07-26) after an empty/malformed body crashed pre_tool_use with an unhandled JSONDecodeError. Any NEW hook endpoint added here must use _safe_json too, not a bare `await request.json()`, to preserve this fail-open guarantee.
server-fastapi-hook-server.name: server-fastapi-hook-server

contracts: record_prompt/record_tool/record_task write to both layers
get(n_events) returns from in-memory cache only (no DB hit at read time)
server-memory-consolidated-timeline.description: Two-layer consolidated context store (SQLite + in-memory cache) answering 'what was I working on?'. Stores prompts, MCP tool calls, and task activations as a chronological event sequence. Write-through: every insert hits both SQLite and the in-memory cache.
invariants: Test sessions (prefixed test-, pytest-, api-test-) are never written to the store
Rolling window capped at 1000 events — oldest deleted on overflow
Cache is hydrated from SQLite at server startup so context survives reloads
server-memory-consolidated-timeline.name: server-memory-consolidated-timeline

contracts: record_tool_from_hook(body) and record_task_from_hook(body) take raw PostToolUse dicts
A Bash call is recorded as a 'git commit' event only when _is_git_commit(command) is true; the recorded args are the comma-joined task:<id> references found anywhere in the command, or None
server-memory-tool-recording.description: Hook payload helpers that extract and record tool calls from raw PostToolUse payloads. MCP tools recorded with compact JSON args. Read/Edit/Write recorded with file_path. Bash only recorded for version-control operations — decided by hooks.gates._is_git_commit, imported rather than reimplemented (task:e247268e). tasks__set_active recorded as task type not tool type, from ANY MCP server providing that name — this is an observability layer, not a rule enforcer, so recording activity from other servers' tasks is correct. Title used to be resolved authoritatively from proj_tasks.db (task:87ec7876 removed that lookup, _title_for_task); it now comes only from the tool's own response, which was already the fallback path for any task the DB lookup missed.
invariants: record_task_from_hook never queries a task store — title comes from the tool response only

Commit detection is SHARED with GitCommitGate via hooks.gates._is_git_commit, never a local copy. Until task:e247268e this module imported the gate's old _GIT_COMMIT_RE, and so silently inherited its false positives: any Bash call merely containing the word 'commit' after a git subcommand was recorded as a 'git commit' timeline event. Historical rows written before that fix include phantom commits, so the timeline is not trustworthy as a commit log for that period.
A change to what counts as a commit changes this module's output too, not just what the gate blocks — the two consumers cannot be reasoned about independently.
server-memory-tool-recording.name: server-memory-tool-recording

contracts: get_session_graph(session_id: str = '') -> a compiled, checkpointer-backed StateGraph, production or test depending on session_id prefix
session-graph-test-production-routing.description: get_session_graph(session_id) is the single chokepoint every hook entry point (run_session, run_gate, run_post_tool, run_stop, prewarm_session) already calls to obtain the compiled LangGraph StateGraph. Since task:b63088a1, it also decides WHICH of two graph instances to return based on session_id's prefix, isolating integration-test checkpoint traffic from the shared production MemorySaver without changing any endpoint URL or code path.
invariants: Any session_id starting with TEST_SESSION_PREFIX ('integration-test-') routes to _test_graph, a separate lazily-built graph/MemorySaver instance; every other session_id (including '') routes to the production _graph, exactly as before this routing existed.

Both _graph and _test_graph are built lazily on first use via the identical build_session_graph(checkpointer=MemorySaver()) pattern — no special-casing between them except which module-level global gets populated.

A checkpoint written under a test-prefixed session_id is genuinely invisible to the production graph, not just conventionally separated — they are two distinct MemorySaver instances with independent .storage dicts.
No eviction/cleanup logic exists for _test_graph and none is needed: both graphs reset to empty on every server restart, since MemorySaver has no persistence and none is intended for either.

Callers that reference the underlying singleton directly (sg._graph) rather than through get_session_graph(session_id) will NOT get isolation-aware routing — hooks/server.py's session_detail endpoint and hooks/dispatcher.py's _handle_session_end both had to be updated to route through get_session_graph(session_id) (or check the correct global explicitly) for the isolation guarantee to hold end-to-end.
session-graph-test-production-routing.name: session-graph-test-production-routing

contracts: get_current_session() -> {session_id, turn} or {} if no checkpoint exists anywhere
get_active_session() -> {task_id, title, session_id, turn} or {} if no active task on the latest checkpoint
session-state-latest-checkpoint-lookup.description: get_current_session/get_active_session back GET /session/current and GET /session/active — the only signals available for 'what session am I in' before any thread_id is known. Both use _latest_checkpoint_tuple() to find the single most-recently-written checkpoint across all threads. get_active_session used to resolve the checkpoint's task id against proj_tasks.db to drop done/abandoned tasks (task:87ec7876) — that made it look authoritative about a fact this repo no longer owns. It now reports the checkpoint verbatim: a stale checkpoint can name a finished task, which is correct for a session echo feeding a UI endpoint rather than a second active-task pointer with nothing to reconcile it against.
invariants: Never resolves active_task_id against any task store — reports the checkpoint as-is
session-state-latest-checkpoint-lookup.name: session-state-latest-checkpoint-lookup

contracts: toon_cell(value) -> str: stringifies value, wraps in double quotes with internal quotes doubled if it contains a comma, newline, or quote character
rows_to_toon(rows: list[dict]) -> str: returns 'rows[0]{}:' for an empty list, otherwise 'rows[N]{field1,field2,...}:' header line followed by one two-space-indented comma-joined line per row
toon-encoding-shared-module.description: Shared TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation) encoder for MCP tool responses that return arrays of uniform-schema dicts. Originally extracted from src/tools/hooks.py (task:d2165715) so src/tools/tasks.py's handle_list (task:4b5bf21f) could reuse it without duplicating the comma/quote/newline escaping logic. That second consumer no longer exists — src/tools/tasks.py was deleted by task:87ec7876 — so as of 2026-08-01 the only production caller is src/tools/hooks.py's handle_read_logs_sqlite. The module is kept as a standalone unit (rather than folded back into hooks.py) because it is independently unit-tested in tests/test_toon.py and is the natural home for any future TOON-emitting tool.
invariants: Only worth using for a list of dicts sharing the same keys, returned to an LLM caller rather than a human reading raw output — nested/heterogeneous data (e.g. concept_store/concepts.json entries) loses to plain JSON under TOON, so this is not a blanket replacement for JSON responses repo-wide.

rows_to_toon() uses the FIRST row's keys as the header and does not fill in missing keys for later rows — callers MUST normalize every row to an identical, consistent key set before calling it, or the tabular header will not match later rows. (Historical example, now deleted: handle_list in src/tools/tasks.py did this for the optional _context_only field, defaulting it to False on every row.)

Any existing MCP tool being defaulted to TOON output must have its internal (non-MCP, in-process Python) callers grepped for and updated to pass format="json" explicitly — the unit test suite alone is not sufficient signal, since unit tests typically only exercise the tool module directly, not other in-process callers integrating with it. (Historical example, both modules now deleted: task:4b5bf21f found hooks/ui/routes.py calling tasks.py's handle_list() directly in 5 places expecting list[dict], caught only by the integration suite at deploy time, not the unit gate.)
toon-encoding-shared-module.name: toon-encoding-shared-module

contracts: LoadTaskCodeNode.__call__ resolves .code_embeddings.tvim/.meta.json from Path(state['cwd']) first
LoadRelatedCommitsNode._resolve_diff_index(cwd) resolves .diff_embeddings.tvim/.meta.json from Path(cwd) first, returns (index, meta)
Both fall back to a hardcoded claude-hooks default path only when no index exists at the cwd-derived path
ups-nodes-cwd-first-repo-resolution.description: Repeated pattern across UPS task-context fan-out nodes: any node resolving a repo-scoped index/resource must try state['cwd']'s repo first, falling back to a hardcoded default repo (claude-hooks) only if nothing exists at cwd. LoadTaskCodeNode (langchain_learning/nodes/load_task_code.py) established this; LoadRelatedCommitsNode (langchain_learning/nodes/load_related_commits.py) was fixed to match it in task:4b7ccfe8 after being found to always query claude-hooks' diff index regardless of the active task's actual repo.
invariants: A task can be activated from any repo, not just claude-hooks — a node that skips the cwd check silently returns data from the wrong repo instead of failing loudly or returning empty
cwd-derived resolution is tried first and only falls back to the default repo path if the cwd-scoped resource is missing, never the other way around
New UPS nodes that read a repo-local file/index (TurboVec .tvim, git log, etc.) must follow this same resolution order
ups-nodes-cwd-first-repo-resolution.name: ups-nodes-cwd-first-repo-resolution
